basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 12:1 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 154. Quid in tribus illis egressionibus intelligendum est, in quibus praecipitur a'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 154. Quid in tribus illis egressionibus intelligendum est, in quibus praecipitur a Domino Abrahae ut egrediatur de terra sua et de cognatione sua, et de domo patris sui (Gen. XII, 1)?-- Resp. Nihil aliud, nisi nobis [ Edit., non] egrediendum esse de terreno homine, et de cognatione vitiorum nostrorum, et de domo patris, id est, mundo, qui diaboli domus dicitur, ut in Psalmo: Obliviscere populum tuum et domum patris tui (Psal. XLIV, 11).
